property_summary: Only transactions originating from the jojoTeam address cannot create a new EmergencyOracle via c.newEmergencyOracle when the caller is a different EOAs (i.e., newEmergencyOracle can only be successfully invoked by the externally owned jojoTeam account, not by a contract call).
Only the jojoTeam address can successfully call newEmergencyOracle (calls from others revert), so newEmergencyOracle succeeds iff msg.sender == jojoTeam.

For any caller address chosen as the owner argument when creating a new EmergencyOracle via newEmergencyOracle, the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's owner (the deployer passed to EmergencyOracle constructor) equals the msg.sender that created the new oracle; the mutant that passes address(this) breaks this by making the stored owner different from msg.sender for some inputs.

For any caller address X (the jojoTeam) that invokes newEmergencyOracle, the newly deployed EmergencyOracle's owner equals X (the msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) as owner causes the deployed oracle's owner to be different from msg.sender for some caller X, so there exists an input where the stored owner != caller.

For any jojoTeam caller that invokes newEmergencyOracle, the deployed EmergencyOracle's owner equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) as owner causes for some caller the deployed oracle's owner to differ from msg.sender, violating this rule.

For every jojoTeam caller that calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the newly deployed EmergencyOracle's owner equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that uses address(this) as owner causes the deployed oracle's owner to differ from the caller for some caller addresses.

For any jojoTeam caller that calls newEmergencyOracle(description), the deployed EmergencyOracle's owner (as returned by its public owner() getter) equals the caller (msg.sender); the mutant that passes address(this) as the constructor owner causes the deployed oracle's owner to be address(this) instead of the caller for some callers, breaking the rule.

For any caller equal to jojoTeam, when they call newEmergencyOracle(description) the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed owner argument equals the msg.sender (the jojoTeam caller); the mutant emits jojoTeam instead which can differ when msg.sender != jojoTeam (e.g., when jojoTeam is a separate address and the call is proxied via that address).

For any caller A that is approved as jojoTeam on the contract, when A calls newEmergencyOracle(description) the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first indexed owner equals the actual msg.sender (the caller) — the mutant incorrectly emits the stored jojoTeam address instead, so when the call is proxied through a forwarding contract the emitted owner differs.

For any caller X who is the jojoTeam and any arbitrary address P that X forwards through (a proxy), when X invokes newEmergencyOracle through that proxy the referenced contract C should record the emitted owner as the actual msg.sender of the call (the proxy) — the mutant wrongly emits the stored jojoTeam address instead, so there exists a proxy caller for which the emitted owner differs.

Whenever jojoTeam calls newEmergencyOracle(description) (i.e., msg.sender == jojoTeam), the emitted NewEmergencyOracle event's first argument must equal msg.sender (the immediate caller); the mutant instead always emits the stored jojoTeam address which can differ when the call is made via a forwarding contract, so the mutant will break this rule for some forwarding caller addresses.

For every caller addr (jojoTeam) invoking newEmergencyOracle, the created EmergencyOracle.owner (read via owner()) equals the immediate msg.sender passed to the EmergencyOracle constructor (the caller of newEmergencyOracle); the mutant still deploys with the caller as owner but emits the stored jojoTeam in the event, so observing the oracle's owner getter distinguishes the mutant from the reference when a forwarder/proxy address calls newEmergencyOracle on behalf of jojoTeam.
